question: For a merge-queue entry behind another, is `github.event.merge_group.base_sha` the commit its group is built on, the head of the group ahead of it, and not the tip of `main`; and is it, every time, the parent of the group's own head?
pass: Yes to both: the base a Lens reads from is what `main` will be when the entry merges (decision 0023). If it is the tip of `main`, an entry behind another is judged against rules the entry ahead may change, and is judged again once that one merges. Written before the read, in the design's row. Read only, as the Maintainer, from combsmith/software-factory's own merge queue, which builds five groups at once; the canary's builds one, and changing that is the Maintainer's setting.

request.call: GET /repos/combsmith/software-factory/actions/workflows/verify.yml/runs?event=merge_group&per_page=100, every page (of each run, its id, times, branch, head and conclusion are kept)
GET /repos/combsmith/software-factory/commits/{head_sha} for each of those heads (of each answer, its parents are kept, by head)

gh run view --job {job} --log, for the job commits of each group built while the group ahead still ran, 50 of them (of each log, what the job's env says of the event is kept: BASE_SHA and HEAD_SHA, which verify.yml sets from merge_group.base_sha and head_sha)
